newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-COURIER BOUNCED, SAMPRAS SURVIVES IN PHILADELPHIA. [CORRECTED 04:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COURIER BOUNCED, SAMPRAS SURVIVES IN PHILADELPHIA. [CORRECTED 04:50 GMT]

text.p: Second-seeded defending champion Jim Courier was sent packing from the Advanta Championships by South African Grant Stafford on Thursday, but top seed Pete Sampras survived his second round challenge.
The 18th-ranked Courier rallied to force a third set only to fall 6-3 5-7 6-2 to the 78th-ranked Stafford.
World number one Sampras, a two-time winner of this event, struggled with his usually devastating serve before holding off 38th-ranked Jonas Bjorkman of Sweden 7-5 7-6 (corrects score from 7-6 7-6).
"He was returning very well, especially off of my second serve," said Sampras, who picked up his ninth Grand Slam title at the Australian Open last month.
"He was very capable of beating me tonight. This was one of those matches you just want to get through."
That Sampras got through brought a major sigh of relief from tournament officials, who would have been left without a seeded player had Bjorkman prevailed.
Sixth-seeded Australian Todd Woodbridge was crushed 6-2 6-0 by 55th-ranked Byron Black of Zimbabwe in another second round match.

In the quarter-finals, Sampras takes on 129th-ranked qualifier Doug Flach; Stafford plays 66th-ranked Sandon Stolle of Australia; Black faces 60th-ranked Pat Rafter of Australia; and 61st-ranked American Jonathan Stark meets 88th-ranked qualifier Sjeng Schalken of the Netherlands.
Stafford played extremely well against Courier, but the American succumbed as much to fatigue from his own excessive globe trotting of recent weeks.
Over the last six weeks, Courier has played in Qatar, Australia, Florida, Brazil, Dubai, Belgium and Pennsylvania.
"Maybe it's a blessing in disguise that I go out of here early," said Courier. "It will give me time to relax and recharge the batteries."
Courier seemed always to be facing an uphill battle, even in the second set, which he won. "I thought I played okay today, but the guy was playing off his perch," Courier said.

When Courier won the final three games of the second set, it seemed he had seized the momentum to carry him through the third. But it was Stafford who broke away in the final set with a scorching forehand winner for a key service break in the fourth game.
Stafford won match with another service break when he hit a forehand volley that nicked the top of the net and bounced onto Courier's side.
"Against a guy as experienced as Jim, it's tough to pull the third set off," Stafford said. "The third set, I got the break and went from there. I kept my composure."
Sampras also looked to be facing an early exit, falling behind to the 38th-ranked Bjorkman in both sets.
The Swede was up 2-1 and 5-3 with service breaks in the first set and held leads of 4-3 and 6-5 thanks to breaks in the second.
Despite losing his serve four times, however, Sampras closed it out in pure Sampras style -- serving four aces in the 7-2 tie-break, including on the final two points.
